subject: Procurement path evaluation & marketplace preference — FinServ Analytics
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@finserv.io>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finserv.io>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: procurement path and billing preference

Hi Sofia — great to speak earlier. Thanks for walking us through the use case and the internal buying process. Per our call, I wanted to capture the options we discussed and a few clarifying questions so we can map the fastest path to purchase.

Summary of options we discussed:
- AWS Marketplace subscription (preferred if possible) — you mentioned finance would prefer marketplace billing to avoid vendor setup.
- Direct contract / PO (Net 45) — procurement/legal may require an MSA and purchase order.
- Credit card / P-card for pilot (smaller trial) — finance could approve one-off card payments for pilots.

Questions for you (to confirm):
1) Would an AWS Marketplace listing that invoices monthly be sufficient for the production rollout, or is procurement insisting on a PO for the first purchase?
2) If we provide an MSA + SOW, would procurement accept Net 45 payment terms? Any chance of Net 30?
3) Any required vendor info (tax ID, W-9) or a supplier intake form we should pre-populate?

Attached: Redwood_SOW_template_v1.pdf (SOW draft) and AWS_Marketplace_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (rough checklist for marketplace listing). If marketplace is viable, we can prioritize onboarding and get you a private offer (if needed).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm marketplace vs PO preference and any mandatory forms.
- I loop in our partnerships and finance leads to confirm timeline for listing or PO acceptance.

Thanks — I can be flexible on next call timing next week to align all stakeholders.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(vivek@redwood.com)

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_template_v1.pdf (SOW), AWS_Marketplace_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (checklist)

From: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@finserv.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finserv.io>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement path and billing preference

Vivek — thanks for the recap and for sending those docs. Short answers below: 

1) Marketplace preference: Finance would strongly prefer AWS Marketplace for subscription billing because it simplifies our vendor onboarding and leverages our existing agreement with AWS. If Redwood can list and provide a private offer or ISA, that will be the fastest path to production.

2) PO terms: If Marketplace is not available in time, procurement will accept a PO. Our standard is Net 45, and legal will expect an MSA + SOW (your SOW template is helpful). We do sometimes push for Net 60 on larger vendors, but for a new vendor Net 45 is typical.

3) Vendor intake: We will need a completed supplier intake form (I attached our vendor intake checklist in a separate thread to procurement). Required items: Tax ID/EIN, W-9, primary contact, and a copy of your MSA; if you plan to be a reseller via marketplace, indicate that on the intake.

Two additional notes: 
- Pilot billing: Finance is open to p-card for a pilot under $15k, but any production rollout should go through Marketplace or PO.
- Marketplace timing: It can take 3–6 weeks to list if you need marketplace procurement integrations and contract reviews; private offers can shorten that if you already have a listing.

Happy to jump on a short call with procurement next week to align.

Best,
Sofia Ruiz
Head of Procurement, FinServ Analytics
sofia.ruiz@finserv.io
